options: Yes, because it gives the main reason that people join the library.
No, because its casual tone and sweeping claim do not fit the passage.
No, because it repeats information already given in sentence 3.
No, because it should be placed at the start of the passage.
Yes, because it supports the estimate given in sentence 9 with additional data.
questions.explanation: The passage is informative and measured; "honestly" and "kind of a waste" are chatty, and the claim is an unsupported generalization. It offers no data and repeats nothing from sentence 3.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the main purpose of the second paragraph (sentences 6 through 10)?
options: To show the work that keeps the library running and what it has achieved
To persuade readers to volunteer at the library's second location
To explain why most households rarely use the tools they own
To describe the history of the building where the library opened
To compare the tool library with a library that lends books
questions.explanation: The paragraph describes volunteers' work, the classes and the library's results. Household tool use belongs to the first paragraph, and there is no comparison or call to volunteer.

questions.stem:
In sentence 10 (reproduced below), the writer wants to stress that the organizers plan to expand despite an obstacle. Which of the following versions of the underlined portion best does this? Choice A keeps the sentence as it is.

They hope to open a second location, __even though they have not yet found__ a building.
options: even though they have not yet found
because they have not yet found
so that they have not yet found
and so they have found
unless they have already managed to find
questions.explanation: "Even though" already signals planning despite an obstacle, so the sentence is best as it is. "Because" and "so that" create false cause and purpose, and the last two change the meaning.

questions.stem: A student is researching what daily life was like for soldiers during the Civil War. Which of the following is a primary source?
options: A textbook chapter on the Civil War published in 2010
An encyclopedia entry summarizing the major battles of the war
A letter a soldier wrote to his family from camp in 1863
A historian's book that analyzes soldiers' diaries from the war
A documentary film made in the 1990s about Civil War camps
questions.explanation: A primary source was created by someone who took part in or witnessed the events. A soldier's letter from 1863 qualifies; the others are later accounts that interpret the past.

questions.stem:
Brandt, Tomas. *A Short History of Maps*. 2nd ed., Northfield Press, 2018.

In the citation above, Northfield Press is the
options: editor of the second edition
title of the series
library that owns the book
publisher of the book
author of the book
questions.explanation: In this book citation the author comes first, then the italicized title, the edition, the publisher and the year. Northfield Press is the publisher.

questions.stem: A student needs current statistics on how many households in the United States have home internet service. Which of the following should the student check first when judging a website that reports such figures?
options: Whether the website's address is short and easy to remember
How many paragraphs of text appear on the page
Whether the website uses large and colorful charts
How many other websites have linked to the page
When the figures were collected and who collected them
questions.explanation: For current statistics, the date of the data and the reliability of its source matter most. Design, length, popularity and a short address say nothing about accuracy.

questions.stem: A student copies a sentence from an online article into a research paper, changes two words and does not name the source. Which of the following best describes what the student has done?
options: Quoted correctly, because the sentence appears in the paper exactly once
Paraphrased correctly, because some of the words in the sentence were changed
Used common knowledge, because the article was freely available online
Summarized fairly, because only a single sentence from the article was used
Plagiarized, because the wording and idea came from a source that was not credited
questions.explanation: Changing a few words does not make writing one's own, and any borrowed idea or wording must be credited. Free availability online does not make something common knowledge.

questions.stem: A school club has 18 members, and the ratio of sixth graders to seventh graders in the club is 2 to 1. How many members are sixth graders?
questions.explanation: The ratio has 2 + 1 = 3 parts, so each part is 18 / 3 = 6 members. Sixth graders are 2 parts: 12.

questions.stem: Five friends ran a race in 24, 27, 30, 21 and 33 minutes. What was their mean time?
options: 24 minutes
30 minutes
27 minutes
135 minutes
33 minutes
questions.explanation: The total is 24 + 27 + 30 + 21 + 33 = 135 minutes, and 135 / 5 = 27 minutes. 135 is the total, not the mean.

questions.stem: If $\frac{x}{4} + 3 = 7$, what is the value of $x$? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: Subtract 3: $\frac{x}{4} = 4$. Multiply by 4: $x = 16$.

questions.stem: A jacket that normally costs \$80 is on sale for 15% off. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: 15% of \$80 is 0.15 x 80 = \$12, so the sale price is 80 - 12 = \$68. \$92 adds the discount instead of subtracting it.

questions.stem: What is the median of the data set 18, 4, 11, 25, 9, 14, 30? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: In order: 4, 9, 11, 14, 18, 25, 30. With seven values, the median is the fourth, 14.

questions.stem: A line passes through the points $(2, 5)$ and $(6, 13)$. What is the slope of the line?
questions.explanation: Slope is the change in $y$ over the change in $x$: $\frac{13 - 5}{6 - 2} = \frac{8}{4} = 2$. Flipping the fraction gives $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.stem: What is $2\frac{1}{3} + 1\frac{3}{4}$?
questions.explanation: With a common denominator of 12: $\frac{1}{3} = \frac{4}{12}$ and $\frac{3}{4} = \frac{9}{12}$, which add to $\frac{13}{12} = 1\frac{1}{12}$. Then $2 + 1 + 1\frac{1}{12} = 4\frac{1}{12}$.

questions.stem: A fair number cube has faces numbered 1 through 6. What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
questions.explanation: Only 5 and 6 are greater than 4, so the probability is $\frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3}$. "Greater than 4" does not include 4.

questions.stem: A family bought 7 tickets to a show. Adult tickets cost \$12 and child tickets cost \$8, and the family paid \$68 in all. How many adult tickets did they buy?
questions.explanation: Let $a$ be adult tickets, so there are $7 - a$ child tickets: $12a + 8(7 - a) = 68$. Then $4a + 56 = 68$, so $a = 3$. Check: 3 adults cost \$36 and 4 children cost \$32, \$68 in all.

questions.stem: A pump fills a tank at a constant rate of 12 gallons per minute. How many minutes will it take to fill a 300-gallon tank? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: Time equals amount divided by rate: 300 / 12 = 25 minutes.

questions.stem:
The table shows the number of visitors to a park each day of a long weekend.

| Day | Visitors |
|---|---|
| Friday | 350 |
| Saturday | 820 |
| Sunday | 640 |
| Monday | 410 |

What percent of the weekend's visitors came on Saturday? Round to the nearest whole percent.
questions.explanation: The weekend total is 350 + 820 + 640 + 410 = 2,220. Saturday's share is 820 / 2,220, about 0.369, or 37%.

questions.stem: A plumber charges a \$45 visit fee plus \$30 for each hour of work. Which expression gives the total charge, in dollars, for $h$ hours of work?
questions.explanation: The \$45 fee is charged once, and \$30 is charged for each of the $h$ hours: $45 + 30h$.

questions.stem: What is the value of the digit 6 in 82.064?
options: 6 tenths
6 ones
6 tens
6 hundredths
6 thousandths
questions.explanation: The places to the right of the decimal point are tenths (0), hundredths (6) and thousandths (4).

questions.stem: A scatterplot shows the outdoor temperature each day (horizontal axis) and the number of hot drinks a cafe sold that day (vertical axis). As the temperature rises, the points fall steadily. Which of the following is the best description?
options: A negative association: warmer days go with fewer hot drinks sold
A positive association: warmer days go with more hot drinks sold
Proof that cold weather is the only cause of the cafe's hot drink sales
No association between temperature and hot drinks sold
A positive association that only appears on cold days
questions.explanation: Points that fall as the horizontal value rises show a negative association. A scatterplot alone cannot prove what causes the sales.

questions.stem: Two angles together form a straight line. One angle is 3 times as large as the other. What is the measure of the smaller angle?
options: 45 degrees
30 degrees
90 degrees
135 degrees
60 degrees
questions.explanation: Angles that form a straight line add to 180 degrees: $x + 3x = 180$, so $x = 45$. The larger angle is 135 degrees.

questions.stem: What is the least common multiple of 12 and 18?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 18 are 18, 36, 54 and so on; 36 is the first that 12 also divides. From prime factors: $12 = 2^2 \cdot 3$ and $18 = 2 \cdot 3^2$, so the LCM is $2^2 \cdot 3^2 = 36$. 6 is the greatest common factor.

questions.stem: A spinner has four equal sections colored red, blue, green and yellow. If it is spun twice, what is the probability that it lands on red both times?
questions.explanation: Each spin lands on red with probability $\frac{1}{4}$, and the spins are independent, so the probability is $\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{16}$.

questions.stem: A circular table has a diameter of 10 feet. Using 3.14 for $\pi$, what is the circumference of the table? (Circumference $= \pi d$)
options: 62.8 feet
15.7 feet
78.5 feet
31.4 feet
314 feet
questions.explanation: $C = \pi d = 3.14 \times 10 = 31.4$ feet. 78.5 is the area, $\pi r^2$ with $r = 5$, and 62.8 uses 20 in place of the diameter.

questions.stem: Which of the following numbers are divisible by both 3 and 4? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: A number divisible by 3 and 4 is divisible by 12. 48 = 12 x 4, 84 = 12 x 7 and 132 = 12 x 11. 64 is not divisible by 3, and 90 is not divisible by 4.

questions.stem: For the data set 3, 5, 5, 6, 8, 9, 13, which of the following statements are true? Select all that apply.
options: The mean is less than the median.
The range is 10.
The mean is 6.
The median is 6.
The mode is 5.
questions.explanation: 5 appears twice, so it is the mode. The fourth of seven values is 6, the median. The range is 13 - 3 = 10. The values sum to 49, so the mean is 7, which is greater than the median.

questions.stem: A 13-foot ladder leans against a wall with its base 5 feet from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach? (In a right triangle, $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$.)
options: 14 feet
12 feet
18 feet
9 feet
8 feet
questions.explanation: The ladder is the hypotenuse: $5^2 + h^2 = 13^2$, so $h^2 = 169 - 25 = 144$ and $h = 12$ feet.

questions.stem: Which value of $n$ shows that the statement "If $n$ is a whole number, then $n^2 > n$" is false?
questions.explanation: For $n = 1$, $n^2 = 1$, which is not greater than 1, so the statement fails. (It also fails for 0.) For 2, 3, 5 and 10 the square is larger.

questions.stem: A line graph shows a city's monthly rainfall. From January to April the line rises from 2 inches to 5 inches, from April to July it falls to 1 inch, and from July to October it rises to 4 inches. During which of the following periods did the monthly rainfall decrease the whole time?
options: January to April
January to October
April to July
January to July
July to October
questions.explanation: Rainfall fell only between April (5 inches) and July (1 inch). January to July ends lower than it starts, but rainfall rose for the first three months of it.

questions.stem: An aquarium shaped like a rectangular box is 20 inches long, 10 inches wide and 12 inches tall. How many cubic inches of water does it hold when it is filled to a depth of 9 inches? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: The water forms a box 20 by 10 by 9 inches: $20 \times 10 \times 9 = 1{,}800$ cubic inches. The 12-inch height of the tank does not matter.

questions.stem: A runner completes a 5-kilometer race. About how many miles is that? (1 mile is about 1.6 kilometers.)
questions.explanation: Divide kilometers by kilometers per mile: 5 / 1.6 = 3.125, about 3.1 miles. Multiplying (5 x 1.6 = 8) converts in the wrong direction.

questions.stem: The home prices on one street are \$210,000, \$225,000, \$230,000, \$240,000 and \$1,500,000. Which measure best describes a typical home price on the street?
options: The mean, because it uses every price on the street
The median, because one very high price pulls the mean up
The mean, because the median ignores the highest price on the street
The mode, because two of the homes have the same price
The range, because it shows the most expensive home
questions.explanation: One home is far more expensive than the others, so the mean (about \$481,000) is higher than every other price. The median, \$230,000, reflects a typical home. No two prices are equal, so there is no mode.

questions.stem: Which of the following points lie on the line $y = 2x - 1$? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Substitute each $x$: $2(0) - 1 = -1$, $2(2) - 1 = 3$ and $2(3) - 1 = 5$ all match. For $x = 1$, $y = 1$, not 3, and for $x = -1$, $y = -3$, not 1.

questions.stem: A teacher needs 75 copies of a worksheet. The copier prints the worksheets in packs of 20. What is the least number of packs the teacher must print? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: 75 / 20 = 3.75. Three packs give only 60 copies, so the teacher needs 4 packs (80 copies). Here the answer is rounded up.

questions.stem:
Many people assume that a library's most valuable holdings are its rare books. Ask a librarian, though, and you may hear a different answer: the local newspapers, school yearbooks and town records that exist nowhere else. A rare book can usually be found in another library. A town's own history often cannot.

The main point of the statement is that
options: rare books are no longer valuable because most libraries own copies of them
local records may be a library's most valuable holdings because they are irreplaceable
a town's newspapers should be stored in several libraries to keep them safe
most people never visit the rare book collections in their local libraries
librarians would rather collect yearbooks than rare books for their libraries
questions.explanation: The statement contrasts rare books, which other libraries usually hold, with local records that "exist nowhere else," suggesting the local material is the more valuable. It does not say rare books are worthless.

questions.stem:
A gym advertises that its members lose more weight than people who do not belong to a gym, and concludes that joining the gym causes weight loss.

Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the conclusion?
options: The gym's advertisement appeared in several local newspapers.
The gym's membership fee is lower than the fees at other gyms in the city.
The gym added several new exercise machines in the last year.
Many gym members visit the gym more than three times each week.
People who join a gym are often already trying to lose weight in other ways.
questions.explanation: If members are also dieting or changing habits in other ways, those changes rather than the gym may explain their weight loss.

questions.stem:
I have read a great many cookbooks, and most of them promise that their recipes are quick. This one actually delivers. Dinner was on the table in twenty minutes three nights in a row, and nobody complained.

The tone of the statement is best described as
options: pleased
indignant
anxious
sarcastic
nostalgic
questions.explanation: The writer contrasts empty promises with a book that "actually delivers" and reports good results: satisfaction, not sarcasm or anger.

questions.stem:
When the city added protected bike lanes to Grant Avenue, several shop owners warned that losing street parking would drive customers away. A year later, sales on the avenue were up, and a survey found that most shoppers there had arrived on foot, by bus or by bicycle.

Which of the following can be inferred from the statement?
options: The city plans to remove street parking from every avenue.
Sales rose because the city lowered taxes for shops on the avenue.
Street parking was never used by shoppers on Grant Avenue.
Most of the shop owners on Grant Avenue now ride bicycles to work.
The shop owners' warning about losing customers did not come true.
questions.explanation: The owners feared customers would leave, but sales rose and most shoppers did not arrive by car, so the predicted loss did not happen. The statement gives no reason for the rise beyond this and says nothing about other avenues.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what happened in 2015?
options: The vault in Norway was opened for the first time to visiting researchers.
Gene banks in Lebanon and Morocco sent their first seeds to the vault.
The vault's chambers were cooled to about minus 18 degrees Celsius.
A Syrian gene bank moved its entire collection into the Norwegian vault.
Researchers withdrew seeds to rebuild a collection that war had damaged.
questions.explanation: The passage says that in 2015 researchers whose gene bank in Syria had been damaged by war "withdrew seeds to replant their collection in Lebanon and Morocco," the first withdrawal.

questions.stem: As used in the passage, "first resort" most nearly means
options: a vacation spot in the far north
a room that is kept at the lowest temperature
the place one turns to before any other
the final step in a long process
the oldest gene bank in the world
questions.explanation: The vault is "a backup, not a first resort": banks use their own collections first and turn to the vault only if those are lost.

questions.stem:
Seedlings started indoors should be hardened off before they are planted outside. For about a week, place them outdoors in a sheltered spot for a few hours each day, increasing the time gradually. Bring them in at night if temperatures will fall below 50 degrees Fahrenheit.

According to the directions, a gardener hardening off seedlings should
options: keep them outside all night from the first day
plant them outside on the first warm day
bring them in whenever the temperature is above 50 degrees
leave them outside a little longer each day
place them in full sun and wind for a week
questions.explanation: The directions say to put seedlings outside "for a few hours each day, increasing the time gradually" in a sheltered spot, and to bring them in when nights fall below 50 degrees, not above.

questions.stem:
An editor does not write the book, but by questioning, cutting and rearranging, helps the author turn a rough draft into the book it was meant to be.

The editor's role as described is most similar to that of
options: a player who scores the winning point in the game
a reporter who writes about the game the next morning
a coach who helps an athlete improve without playing in the game
a referee who decides which team has won the game
a fan who buys a ticket to watch the team play
questions.explanation: Like an editor, a coach shapes and improves another person's performance without doing the performance itself. A referee judges and a reporter describes; neither helps the performer improve.

questions.stem:
The museum's new policy allows visitors to photograph any object in the permanent collection. Photography remains banned in the special exhibition galleries, where most objects are on loan from other institutions.

The policy suggests that the ban in the special exhibitions most likely exists because
options: objects in the permanent collection are less valuable than loaned ones
the special exhibition galleries are too dark for clear photographs
visitors take too many photographs in the permanent collection galleries
the museum sells photographs of the special exhibitions in its shop
the lending institutions may not permit their objects to be photographed
questions.explanation: The statement links the ban to the fact that most objects there are "on loan from other institutions," which suggests the lenders' rules govern photography. Lighting, sales and value are never mentioned.

questions.stem:
Glass seems solid, yet it has no crystal structure. When most liquids cool, their molecules lock into an orderly pattern. Molten glass cools too quickly for that to happen, so its molecules stay jumbled, as in a liquid, even after it hardens.

The statement is organized mainly by
options: raising a puzzle and then explaining it
telling the story of glass in time order
stating an opinion and then defending it
comparing two kinds of glass by age
listing the steps for making glass
questions.explanation: The first sentence poses a puzzle (solid yet without crystal structure), and the rest explains it by contrasting slow and fast cooling.

questions.stem:
In a survey of 200 teachers at one district's schools, 140 said they use classroom technology every day. Of those 140, 98 said they had received training on the technology in the last two years.

Which of the following is supported by the survey?
options: Every teacher with recent training uses technology every day.
Fewer than half of the teachers surveyed use technology every day.
Training causes teachers to use classroom technology every day.
About half of the teachers surveyed use technology daily and had recent training.
Most teachers in the country use classroom technology every day.
questions.explanation: 98 of 200 teachers, 49 percent, both use technology daily and had recent training, about half. The survey covers one district, shows no cause, and says nothing about trained teachers who do not use technology daily.

questions.stem:
Few inventions have changed daily life as quietly as the shipping container, which cut the cost of moving goods across oceans so sharply that distance almost stopped mattering to trade.

Which of the following best restates the sentence?
options: Daily life changed very little after the shipping container was invented.
The shipping container made ocean shipping so cheap that distance mattered far less in trade.
Shipping containers are used mainly for goods that travel short distances.
Trade between distant countries stopped once shipping containers were invented.
The shipping container was a loud invention that made shipping goods more expensive.
questions.explanation: The sentence says the container lowered shipping costs so much that "distance almost stopped mattering to trade," a large but quiet change. Trade did not stop; it grew easier.

questions.stem:
Choose the underlined part that must be revised to make the sentence correct. If the sentence is correct as written, choose No error.

The candidate __whom__ (A) the committee __believed__ (B) __was__ (C) the best qualified __withdrew__ (D) from the race.
options: whom
believed
was
withdrew
No error
questions.explanation: The pronoun is the subject of "was" (the committee believed he was best qualified), so it must be "who." "The committee believed" only interrupts the clause.

questions.skill: Usage: there is and there are
questions.stem:
Choose the underlined part that must be revised to make the sentence correct. If the sentence is correct as written, choose No error.

The __report__ (A) __lists__ (B) several reasons, and there __is__ (C) more __that__ (D) it does not mention.
options: report
lists
is
that
No error
questions.explanation: After "there," the verb agrees with what follows. "More" here means more reasons, which is plural, so the verb must be "are."

questions.stem:
Choose the underlined part that must be revised to make the sentence correct. If the sentence is correct as written, choose No error.

The new schedule had a __positive__ (A) __affect__ (B) on attendance, __which__ (C) rose __steadily__ (D) all year.
options: positive
affect
which
steadily
No error
questions.explanation: The noun meaning "result" is "effect." "Affect" is usually the verb: the schedule affected attendance.

questions.stem:
Choose the best version of the underlined part of the sentence. Choice A repeats the original; choose it if the original is best.

Marcus finished his chores __early, he went__ to the park with his sister.
options: early, he went
early he went
early, so he went
early, going
early; and he went
questions.explanation: Two complete sentences cannot be joined by a comma alone. "So" adds a connector and shows why he could go.

questions.stem:
Choose the best version of the underlined part of the sentence. Choice A repeats the original; choose it if the original is best.

The secret will stay __between you and I__ until the party.
options: between you and I
between you and me
between yourself and I
among you and I
between I and you
questions.explanation: "Between" is a preposition, so the pronouns that follow it take the object form: between you and me.

questions.stem:
Choose the best version of the underlined part of the sentence. Choice A repeats the original; choose it if the original is best.

Both of the __teachers classrooms were__ painted over the summer.
options: teachers classrooms were
teacher's classrooms were
teachers classroom's were
teachers' classrooms were
teachers' classrooms was
questions.explanation: The classrooms belong to two teachers, so the plural possessive is "teachers'" with the apostrophe after the s. "Classrooms" is plural, so the verb stays "were."

questions.stem:
Which of the following is the most concise revision of the sentence below that keeps its meaning?

In my personal opinion, I think that the meeting should be moved to a later time in the afternoon.
options: I personally think in my opinion that the meeting should move later.
I think the meeting should be moved later in the afternoon.
It is my personal opinion and belief that the meeting should be later.
The meeting, in my opinion, I think, should be moved to a later time.
In my personal opinion, I think the meeting should be moved later.
questions.explanation: "In my personal opinion" and "I think" say the same thing, and "to a later time in" can be shortened to "later in." "I think the meeting should be moved later in the afternoon" keeps the meaning in the fewest words.

questions.stem: The writer wants to add a sentence after sentence 6 to support the point made in sentences 4 through 6. Which of the following best does this?
options: Sea turtles can live for more than fifty years in the wild.
Astronomers often work at observatories built on mountaintops.
Streetlights were first lit by gas in the early 1800s.
Some species of birds migrate thousands of miles each year.
Lights along some beaches now lead many of them inland, away from the water.
questions.explanation: Sentences 4 through 6 show that light pollution harms wildlife. Explaining that beach lighting leads hatchlings away from the sea completes the turtle example. The other choices are true or plausible but off the point.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best way to combine sentences 3 and 4?
options: Astronomers, being the first to complain about this glow, called light pollution, so biologists have since joined them.
Astronomers were the first to complain about this glow, called light pollution, biologists have since joined them.
Astronomers were the first to complain about this glow, called light pollution, but biologists have since joined them.
Astronomers were the first to complain about this glow called light pollution, because biologists have since joined them.
Although biologists have since joined them, astronomers were the first, complaining about this glow called light pollution.
questions.explanation: "But" links the two ideas correctly: astronomers first, biologists since. Joining the clauses with a comma alone makes a comma splice, "so" and "because" invent a cause, and the version opening with "Although" is awkward and blurs the meaning.

questions.stem: In sentence 7, the writer wants a more precise phrase than "fight back." Which of the following best replaces it?
options: do something about the problem
limit the light they send into the sky
turn off every light in town
battle the astronomers' complaints
take a stand against the night
questions.explanation: The next sentence describes shielded streetlights that keep light from going up, so "limit the light they send into the sky" says exactly what the towns do. Turning off every light overstates it, and the others are vague or wrong.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the role of sentence 2 in the passage?
options: It offers a solution to the problem of light pollution.
It gives the main reason that birds migrate at night.
It shows how widespread the problem described in the passage has become.
It introduces the biologists who later joined the astronomers.
It explains how shielded streetlights point light down at the road.
questions.explanation: Sentence 2 turns the history in sentence 1 into a present problem by saying about a third of people can no longer see the Milky Way, which shows its reach.

questions.stem:
The town expected about two hundred people at the festival. ______, more than a thousand arrived, and the food ran out by noon.

Which of the following best fills the blank?
options: For example
Therefore
In addition
Similarly
Instead
questions.explanation: The second sentence reports the opposite of what was expected, so a contrast word is needed. "Instead" signals that contrast; the others signal similarity, an example, a result or an addition.

questions.stem: A student is writing a formal letter to the city council asking for a crosswalk near the school. Which of the following sentences best fits the purpose and audience?
options: Please fix Elm Street, thanks.
Elm Street is a nightmare, and everybody knows the council never cares about kids anyway.
Several students have nearly been struck by cars while crossing Elm Street, and a marked crosswalk would make that crossing safer.
You guys really need to do something about Elm Street before somebody gets totally flattened out there.
Crosswalks are cool, and I think Elm Street would look way better with one.
questions.explanation: A formal request to officials should be respectful and specific, giving a reason. The other sentences are slangy, insulting or vague.

questions.stem: A student searching a library database for articles about school gardens gets thousands of results about gardening in general. Which of the following changes would best focus the search?
options: Search for "gardens" OR "schools"
Search for "gardening" OR "farming" OR "plants" OR "soil"
Search for "plants" instead of "gardens"
Remove every search term except "gardens"
Search for "school gardens" AND "student learning"
questions.explanation: AND requires both ideas in every result, which narrows the search. OR and broader terms widen it, which is the opposite of what the student needs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the best reason to doubt a website's claim that a new supplement improves test scores?
options: The site has a contact form for questions.
The site includes links to other pages.
The site was updated within the last month.
The site is run by the company that sells the supplement.
The site lists the names of its writers.
questions.explanation: A seller has a financial interest in the claim, so its evidence needs independent support. A recent update, named writers and contact details are signs of a better site, not a worse one.

questions.stem: If 2 apples cost as much as 3 oranges, how many oranges cost as much as 50 apples?
questions.explanation: Set up the proportion $\frac{2}{3} = \frac{50}{x}$. Then $2x = 150$, so $x = 75$.

questions.stem: What are the mode and the range of the data set 4, 8, 8, 10, 13?
options: Mode 8, range 9
Mode 10, range 9
Mode 4, range 8
Mode 9, range 8
Mode 8, range 13
questions.explanation: 8 appears most often, so the mode is 8. The range is the greatest value minus the least: 13 - 4 = 9.

questions.stem: If $4(x - 2) = 2x + 6$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Distribute: $4x - 8 = 2x + 6$. Subtract $2x$ and add 8: $2x = 14$, so $x = 7$.

questions.stem: A store marks a \$200 coat down 20%, then takes another 10% off the sale price. What is the final price?
questions.explanation: After 20% off, the price is \$160. Another 10% off \$160 is \$16, leaving \$144. Taking 30% off the original (\$140) overstates the discount.

questions.stem: The mean of three numbers is 20. Two of the numbers are 14 and 25. What is the third number? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: Three numbers with a mean of 20 add to 60. The third is 60 - 14 - 25 = 21.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to $3(2x - 4) - (x - 5)$?
questions.explanation: $3(2x - 4) = 6x - 12$, and $-(x - 5) = -x + 5$. Together: $6x - x - 12 + 5 = 5x - 7$. Forgetting to distribute the minus sign gives $5x - 17$.

questions.stem: What is $3.75 \times 2.4$? Type the number only.
A class has 12 girls and 13 boys. One student's name is drawn at random. What is the probability that the student is a girl, written as a percent?
questions.explanation: 12 of 25 students are girls, and $\frac{12}{25} = 0.48$, or 48%.

questions.stem: A 4-inch by 6-inch photo is enlarged so that its shorter side is 10 inches. If the shape stays the same, how long is the longer side?
options: 24 inches
12 inches
15 inches
14 inches
16 inches
questions.explanation: The scale factor is 10 / 4 = 2.5, so the longer side is $6 \times 2.5 = 15$ inches. Adding 6 inches to each side (giving 12) does not keep the same shape.

questions.stem: A town's population grew at a constant rate from 160,000 in 2015 to 200,000 in 2020. At the same rate, what will the population be in 2023?
questions.explanation: The town gained 40,000 people in 5 years, or 8,000 per year. Three more years add 24,000: 200,000 + 24,000 = 224,000.

questions.stem:
The table shows how 200 students get to school.

| Method | Students |
|---|---|
| Bus | 90 |
| Car | 50 |
| Walk | 40 |
| Bike | 20 |

In a circle graph of the data, how many degrees would the Bus section measure?
questions.explanation: Bus is 90 / 200 = 0.45 of the students, and 0.45 x 360 degrees = 162 degrees.

questions.stem: A garden bed is shaped like a trapezoid with parallel sides of 8 feet and 12 feet and a height of 5 feet. What is its area? (Area of a trapezoid $= \frac{1}{2}(b_1 + b_2)h$)
options: 25 square feet
480 square feet
60 square feet
50 square feet
100 square feet

questions.stem: What is $\frac{1}{4}$ of $\frac{3}{8}$?
questions.explanation: "Of" means multiply: $\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{3}{8} = \frac{3}{32}$.

questions.stem:
A survey asked 80 adults whether they prefer reading print books or e-books.

| | Print | E-book | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Under 40 | 18 | 22 | 40 |
| 40 and over | 28 | 12 | 40 |
| Total | 46 | 34 | 80 |

If a person who prefers e-books is chosen at random, what is the probability that the person is under 40?
questions.explanation: Only the 34 e-book readers count, and 22 of them are under 40: $\frac{22}{34} = \frac{11}{17}$. $\frac{11}{20}$ is the share of under-40s who prefer e-books, a different question.

questions.stem: The sum of two numbers is 30 and their difference is 8. What is the larger number?
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be $x$ and $y$: $x + y = 30$ and $x - y = 8$. Adding the equations gives $2x = 38$, so $x = 19$ and $y = 11$.

questions.stem: What is the prime factorization of 350?
options: $2 \cdot 5 \cdot 35$
$2 \cdot 5^2 \cdot 7$
$2 \cdot 7^2 \cdot 5$
$2^2 \cdot 5 \cdot 7$
questions.explanation: $350 = 2 \cdot 175 = 2 \cdot 5 \cdot 35 = 2 \cdot 5 \cdot 5 \cdot 7$, which is $2 \cdot 5^2 \cdot 7$. 35 and 14 are not prime.

questions.stem: Each value in a data set is increased by 5. Which of the following is true?
options: The mean stays the same and the range increases by 5.
The mean and the range both increase by 5.
Neither the mean nor the range changes.
The mean increases by 5 and the range doubles.
The mean increases by 5 and the range stays the same.
questions.explanation: Adding 5 to every value shifts the whole set up by 5, so the mean (and median) rise by 5. The distance between the greatest and least values does not change, so the range stays the same.

questions.stem: A square has an area of 49 square meters. What is its perimeter, in meters? Type the number only.
questions.explanation: Each side is $\sqrt{49} = 7$ meters, so the perimeter is $4 \times 7 = 28$ meters.

questions.stem: A board is 7 feet 8 inches long. How long is it in inches? (1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.explanation: 7 feet is 7 x 12 = 84 inches, plus 8 inches makes 92 inches.

questions.stem: A survey of 400 voters found that 55% support a new library. Of the supporters, 40% said they would volunteer there. How many of the voters surveyed said they would volunteer?
questions.explanation: 55% of 400 is 220 supporters, and 40% of 220 is 88. 160 is 40% of all 400 voters, which ignores that only supporters were asked.

questions.stem: Three angles of a quadrilateral measure 80, 95 and 110 degrees. What is the measure of the fourth angle?
options: 105 degrees
65 degrees
95 degrees
85 degrees
75 degrees
questions.explanation: The angles of a quadrilateral add to 360 degrees: $360 - (80 + 95 + 110) = 360 - 285 = 75$ degrees.
